title: Half a million UK pupils tackle puzzle challenge

questions.q: This program marks 3 practice puzzles. Which line makes a decision (selection)?
questions.explain: Line 6 is selection because the IF chooses whether to add 3 points, while line 3 repeats code rather than choosing between paths.

questions.q: Which of these are the variables in the program?
questions.explain: score, puzzles and answer all store values that can change, and answer counts too because RECEIVE stores what is typed in it, while "right" is just a piece of text.

questions.q: Which line takes in input from the user?
questions.explain: RECEIVE ... FROM KEYBOARD on line 4 is the input, while line 10 is output because SEND ... TO DISPLAY shows something on the screen.

questions.q: The pupil types right, wrong, right. What does the program display?
questions.explain: Only the two right answers add 3 each, making 6, and it isn't 5 because this program never takes a point away for a wrong answer.

questions.q: What data type is stored in finished?
questions.explain: FALSE is a Boolean value that can only be TRUE or FALSE, and it isn't a string because it has no quotation marks around it.

questions.q: How many times is "Keep going!" displayed?
questions.explain: It runs when minutes is 45, 40 and 35, then stops at 30 because 30 > 30 is FALSE, so it is 3 times and not 4.

questions.q: What kind of loop is this?
questions.explain: WHILE keeps going until a condition stops it, so it is conditional, and it isn't fixed because the code never says a set number of times.

questions.q: How many times is "Next puzzle" displayed?
questions.explain: The inner loop runs 2 times for each of the 4 outer loops, so it is 4 × 2 = 8 and not 4 + 2 = 6.

questions.q: Can this pupil enter? Is age >= 6 AND age <= 19 TRUE or FALSE?
questions.explain: 12 is at least 6 and at most 19, so both sides are TRUE and AND gives TRUE.

questions.q: Is age < 6 OR age > 19 TRUE or FALSE?
questions.explain: 20 > 19 is TRUE, and OR only needs one side to be TRUE, even though age < 6 is FALSE.
10 > 10 is FALSE because 10 is not bigger than itself, and NOT turns FALSE into TRUE.

questions.q: This code tries to swap two puzzle scores. What does it display?
questions.explain: Line 3 puts 7 into a, so line 4 copies that 7 back into b, and it isn't 7 3 because the old 3 was overwritten before it could be saved.

questions.q: A program accepts ages from 6 to 19. Which of these is boundary test data?
questions.explain: 19 is right on the edge of the allowed range, while 12 is normal data because it is safely in the middle.

questions.q: Pattern spotting: level 1 of a puzzle has 1 tile, level 2 has 3, level 3 has 6 and level 4 has 10. How many tiles will level 5 have?
questions.explain: The gap grows by one each time (+2, +3, +4), so the next jump is +5 to make 15, not +4 again to make 14.

questions.q: In Bebras a wrong answer can lose points. What would you do with a puzzle you're not sure about?
options: Come back to it at the end
questions.explain: Talk about it: when is skipping smarter than guessing, and how could you check your answer?
